plans.label: Comparative Politics and Public Policy
plans.concept: Study comparative political institutions, constitutional law, European governance and public economics. Investigate policy questions with quantitative and qualitative methods, supported by international relations and historical inquiry.

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice
GOSGATE102.contribution: Introduces legal institutions, the role of law in society and constitutional and administrative concepts.
GOSGATE102.topics: Legal positivism and empirical and normative perspectives; Common-law and civil-law traditions; Constitutional and administrative law; Criminal law; International law and human rights; Property, contract and tort law; Justice; Law and social control; Law and social change; Race and gender in law; Family law

GOSPOLI111.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
GOSPOLI111.contribution: Examines political authority, justice, ideologies and normative arguments about the welfare state.
GOSPOLI111.topics: Society, rights and political authority; Classical political thought; Sovereignty and political realism; Enlightenment and revolution; Liberalism and conservatism; Feminism; Nationalism; Socialism and communism; Empire, race and decolonization; Welfare state and libertarianism; Neoliberalism; Justice

GOSPOLI112.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
GOSPOLI112.contribution: Compares regimes, parties, representation, constitutions, bureaucracies and policymaking institutions.
GOSPOLI112.topics: Democracy and authoritarianism; Democratization and democratic backsliding; States, nations and nationalism; Constitutions and courts; Executives, legislatures and bureaucracies; Political economy; Parties and party systems; Populism and technocracy; Elections and electoral systems; Political culture and polarization; Political participation; Interest groups and public policy

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.contribution: Introduces incentives, markets and aggregate outcomes as foundations for economic policy.
BENECON111.topics: Supply and demand; Game theory; Rational consumer choice; Individual and market demand; Production and costs; Perfect competition; Aggregate output; Unemployment and inflation; Goods and financial markets; IS-LM model

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: Develops survey design, operationalisation, sampling, research design and statistical inference.
BENGATE102.topics: Scientific inquiry and hypotheses; Operationalization and measurement; Reliability and validity; Survey construction and sampling; Randomized and quasi-experimental designs; Nonexperimental and qualitative research; Descriptive statistics; Sampling distributions and estimation; Hypothesis testing and confidence intervals; Association and regression; Research ethics and anonymous data collection

GOSLAWJ213.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
GOSLAWJ213.contribution: Compares legislatures, executives, courts, constitutional rights and administrative remedies.
GOSLAWJ213.topics: Constitutional origins and fundamental features; Federalism and decentralization; Parliaments and lawmaking; Governments and heads of state; Court systems and judicial review; Constitutional rights; EU constitutional order; Administrative-law functions; Public participation; Administrative remedies; Procedural fairness, discretion and legitimate expectations

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Required personal and academic development; argument, source use and responsible AI also support written work.
ACCPPDE101.topics: Scholarly sources and research questions; Argumentation and thesis statements; Literature synthesis; Academic integrity and referencing; Community engagement; Personal learning goals and reflective learning; Collaborative learning; Self-efficacy; Stress and time management; Responsible use of AI

GOSPOLI212.name: Theory of International Relations
GOSPOLI212.contribution: Explains interactions between states and non-state actors through competing international-relations theories.
GOSPOLI212.topics: International state system and non-state actors; Classical and contemporary geopolitics; Realism and neorealism; Liberalism and neoliberalism; Marxism and world-systems theory; Constructivism and critical theory; Foreign-policy decision-making; War and great-power competition; Colonialism and economic relations; Climate politics; UN Security Council diplomacy

GOSHIST111.name: Modern History
GOSHIST111.contribution: Traces political ideologies and the development of democracy and dictatorship in modern history.
GOSHIST111.topics: Modernity and periodization; Industrialization and reform; Political ideologies and nationalism; Migration and imperialism; National, class, gender and racial identities; World wars; Russian Revolution and Soviet history; Democracy and dictatorship; Cold War; Decolonization; Globalization; Historical visions of the future

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: Adds sociological concepts for understanding inequality, group identities and social institutions.
GOSSOCI111.topics: Sociological imagination and knowledge; Social structure and socialization; Classical social theory; Colonialism and the formation of sociology; Solidarity and modernity; Identity, belonging and othering; Groups and social networks; Capital, class and mobility; Race and gender inequality; Global inequality and migration; Education and labour-market inequality

MCCCOMM111.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
MCCCOMM111.contribution: Develops rhetorical analysis and argumentation, including deliberative speech and delivery.
MCCCOMM111.topics: Greek and Roman rhetoric; Deliberative, forensic and epideictic discourse; Logos, ethos and pathos; Invention, arrangement, style, memory and delivery; Argumentation and fallacies; Tropes and schemes; Stasis and enthymemes; Persuasive speech; Narrative and storytelling; Immersive educational communication

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: Develops exploratory data analysis, integration and visualization, including text and web data.
DISDATA111.topics: Data visualization; Exploratory data analysis; Tidy data; Data transformation and integration; Dates and times; Web data; Text data; Geospatial data; Programming functions; Data-based research questions

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.contribution: Studies public provision, welfare programmes, social insurance, taxation and redistribution.
BENECON311.topics: Role and size of government; Market efficiency and failure; Public goods; Externalities; Efficiency and equity; Public production; Public choice; Public expenditure; Health and education policy; Welfare programs; Social insurance; Taxation and redistribution

BENECON212.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
BENECON212.contribution: Analyzes market power, externalities and the rationale for government intervention.
BENECON212.topics: Choice under uncertainty; Non-egoistic preferences; Cognitive limitations; Monopoly; Imperfect competition and strategic behaviour; Labour markets; Capital markets; General equilibrium; Market efficiency; Externalities; Government intervention

GOSLAWJ312.name: Foundations of European Union Law
GOSLAWJ312.contribution: Studies EU competences, rights, citizenship and enforcement of EU law.
GOSLAWJ312.topics: European integration and institutions; EU legal sources and fundamental rights; Competences, subsidiarity and proportionality; Supremacy; Direct and indirect effect; State liability; Preliminary rulings; Review of EU acts and enforcement; EU citizenship; Free movement of persons, workers and goods; Establishment and services; Digital-market regulation and green transition

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis
GOSPOLI312.contribution: Analyzes public policymaking across levels and develops policy memos through a substantive case.
GOSPOLI312.topics: Investigates public policy in the context of globalization. Uses a case study on sugar to examine policy‑making phases and alternative conceptualisations across national and international arenas. Students write policy memos.

GOSPOLI311.name: European Union Politics
GOSPOLI311.contribution: Analyzes EU institutions, interest representation, legislative decision-making and implementation.
GOSPOLI311.topics: European integration; EU institutions and decision rules; EU legitimacy and democracy; Public opinion; Parties and European Parliament; Interest representation and lobbying; Agenda setting; EU legislation and implementation; MEP roles and committee behaviour; Political ideology and amendments; Policy salience

BENECON211.name: International Macroeconomics
BENECON211.contribution: Explains open-economy policy, employment and fiscal and monetary choices.
BENECON211.topics: Goods and financial markets; Labour markets; Phillips curve; IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models; Economic growth; Saving and capital accumulation; Technological progress; Expectations; Open-economy macroeconomics; Fiscal and monetary policy; Business cycles and economic crises

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: Examines persuasion, framing, argument and communication ethics.
MCCCOMM311.topics: Persuasion models and psychology; Ethics of persuasion; Coactive persuasion; Verbal and nonverbal communication; Message framing; Argumentation; Cognitive shortcuts and nudging; Science and sustainability communication; Circular lifestyles; Community-engaged communication

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.contribution: Adds model validation and prediction techniques for empirical inquiry, with no claim of a dedicated political analytics module.
DISDATA211.topics: Prediction and model accuracy; Regression and classification; Resampling and validation; Model selection and regularization; High-dimensional data; Nonlinear regression; Tree-based learning; Support vector methods; Dimension reduction; Unsupervised learning; Feature engineering

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.contribution: Uses regression, instrumental variables and inference to assess causal and predictive claims.
BENECON312.topics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

GOSLAWJ212.name: Introduction to Public International Law
GOSLAWJ212.contribution: Explores treaties, jurisdiction, international institutions and how domestic courts interact with international law.
GOSLAWJ212.topics: Sources and theories of international law; Treaty law; International legal subjects; Jurisdiction and immunities; Domestic courts and international law; State responsibility; Use of force; UN reform; Armed conflict and international criminal law; International human rights and economic law; Environmental law; Self-determination; Third World Approaches to International Law; Soft law, compliance and effectiveness; Global environmental treaties

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: Develops interviews, observation, coding and qualitative interpretation with attention to research ethics.
GOSSOCI212.topics: Qualitative knowledge and research design; Ethics, positionality and reflexivity; Mixed methods; Participatory research; Interview and focus-group approaches; Ethnography and participant observation; Documentary and archival sources; Visual and participatory media; Coding and thematic interpretation; Qualitative research dissemination

GOSHIST312.name: Researching the “American Century”
GOSHIST312.contribution: Develops question formulation, source criticism and extended historical argument through research on the American Century.
GOSHIST312.topics: Guides students through the full arc of historical inquiry, from formulating research questions to engaging critically with sources. Emphasises methodological rigour and interdisciplinary thinking and culminates in a substantial research paper.

alignment.vu: Comparative Politics, Democracy and Rule of Law, and Netherlands in Europe
alignment.ucr: GOSPOLI112, GOSLAWJ213 and GOSPOLI311 give real comparative, legal and EU overlap. The Dutch national case and institutional sequence remain distinct.

alignment.vu: Public Management and Economy, Market and Government
alignment.ucr: GOSPOLI312 contributes public policymaking and BENECON311 contributes welfare and public finance. UCR does not reproduce the dedicated management module.

alignment.vu: Two research projects in National Politics and Government
alignment.ucr: BENGATE102, GOSSOCI212 and BENECON312 build survey, qualitative and empirical methods. GOSHIST312 offers substantial historical inquiry with a different subject and research method. Neither reproduces the two politics projects or thesis.

MCCCOMM111 and MCCCOMM311 add oral argument and persuasion, MCCCOMM211 adds discourse analysis, the media courses add representation and platform analysis, and DISARIN111 adds accountability and AI ethics. The option does not claim a VU media specialisation or reproduce VU’s political-writing assignment.

findings: Introduced Introduction to Economics in the first term in both plans. In the closest plan, Theory of International Relations and Public Policy Analysis replace Criminal Law and Ethics, while data science moves to term three. In the communication plan, Public Policy Analysis replaces a creative writing laboratory to provide policy writing.
The plans have materially different emphasis and remain provisional. Neither is a public comparison without the final-year basis. No additional plan has been selected.
